title: Season standings double-count every fixture for seasons 2012-2019 (overlapping Serie A datasets not deduplicated)
evidence: data_loader.py:85-98 concatenates Brasileirao_Matches.csv (2012-2022) and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (2003-2019) without dedup; verified overlap = seasons 2012-2019, 380 duplicate fixtures each. server.py:176 filters competition via substring 'brasileirão', matching both 'Brasileirão Serie A' (data_loader.py:19) and 'Brasileirão Serie A (Histórico)' (data_loader.py:66). Reproduced: season_standings(2019) selects 760 rows and reports Flamengo 180 pts over 76 games (real 2019: 90 pts / 38 games). Ordering is preserved (uniform 2x) but points/W-D-L/GF-GA are doubled. tests/test_server.py:161-165 only asserts '2019' and 'pts' appear in the output, so the suite cannot catch this.
suggestion: Deduplicate on (date, home_team_norm, away_team_norm) in get_matches(), or drop the 2012-2019 rows from one of the two Serie A sources; add a test asserting a known team's real season points (e.g. Flamengo 2019 = 90) and 38 games played.

title: Same duplicate-fixture defect inflates team_statistics, head_to_head, and the statistical tools over Serie A 2012-2019
evidence: All aggregate tools draw from the same concatenated frame (data_loader.py:98). team_statistics (server.py:56-109), head_to_head (server.py:112-164), match_averages (server.py:338-370), top_scorers_analysis (server.py:280-313), and best_home_record (server.py:373-416) count each 2012-2019 Serie A fixture twice whenever the query spans those seasons. Capabilities R6/R10/R11 are otherwise correctly implemented; the error is inherited from the loader, not the aggregation logic.
suggestion: Fixing the loader dedup (see R9 finding) fixes all of these at once.

title: Match filtering supports season but exposes no explicit date-range parameter
evidence: data_loader.py:141-142 filters by season only; find_matches (server.py:23-53) has no from/to date args. R4 says 'date range and/or season', so season alone satisfies the pinned requirement — noted for completeness.
suggestion: Optionally add date_from/date_to args to find_matches.
